prompt:
A single adult humpback whale, the whole animal in frame, shown as an isolated natural-history reference model on a plain flat mid-grey studio backdrop, nothing else in the image.

View: side three-quarter view from slightly above and in front of its left side, so the head, the left flank, the back and both flukes read clearly. The whale fills about 85% of the frame width with clear space around it.

Pose: neutral and straight, body level from snout to tail, mouth closed, tail stock straight, flukes held flat and horizontal. Both long pectoral fins extend outward and slightly down, held clear of the body so a gap of backdrop shows between each fin and the flank; neither fin touches or overlaps the body.

Anatomy (accurate humpback): long narrow pectoral fins about a third of the body length with a scalloped leading edge; rows of knobby tubercles on the top of the head and along the lower jaw; ventral throat grooves running from the chin to the navel; a small dorsal fin set on a low hump two thirds of the way back; broad flukes with a serrated trailing edge.

Skin: dark slate-grey to black back and flanks, mottled white belly and white undersides of the pectoral fins, a few pale clusters of barnacles on the chin and the fin edges, fine scratches and scars on the flanks, a slightly wet matte sheen.

Lighting: soft even studio light from the front and above, no harsh shadows, no rim glow, the backdrop evenly lit. Photographic, physically accurate detail, like a high-end museum specimen model photographed for a 3D scan.

No water, no splash, no ground, no text, no logo, no watermark, no other animals, no people, no border.
